sentence_stem: It is raining outside, so Maria
correct_completion: has got an umbrella in her bag.
full_sentence: It is raining outside, so Maria has got an umbrella in her bag.
acceptable_variants: has got a raincoat with her.
has got an umbrella with her.

options.text: have got an umbrella in her bag.
options.why_wrong: 'Have got' does not agree with the third person singular subject 'Maria'. Use 'has got'.

options.text: has got an umbrella in her bag.
is going to buy an umbrella.
options.why_wrong: This talks about a future plan, but the stem asks for a statement about what Maria already possesses.

options.text: has got a sunny day outside.
options.why_wrong: 'Has got' is used for possession, and a day is not something Maria can own.

grammar_focus: Have got and has got for possession
explanation: 'Has got' expresses possession with a third person singular subject. Portuguese speakers often use one verb form for all subjects, so they may forget to change 'have' to 'has'.
translation: Está a chover lá fora, então a Maria tem um guarda-chuva na bolsa.
